question: How do hyperscale software engineering organizations (Google SRE, Google DeepMind, Microsoft, AWS, OpenAI, Anthropic, Netflix, Meta, Palantir, GitHub, Stripe, Cloudflare, CNCF, OWASP, NIST, SEI CMU) implement automated production readiness reviews, 13-stage release gates, independent verifications, and evidence-first release governance?
scope: Autonomous production readiness assessment, 13-gate release evaluation, 10-state readiness model, release decision engine (APPROVE, REJECT, BLOCK, REMEDIATE, ROLLBACK), verifier independence, and evidence-first release sign-off
claims: Software being built does not mean it is verified; software being verified does not mean it is production-ready; production-ready does not mean release-approved.
Unproven releases must be blocked: NOT PROVEN != APPROVED.
evidence: Google SRE Production Readiness Reviews require explicit non-functional gates (observability, rollback plans, load tests) before production deployment.
Stripe and GitHub progressive delivery engines enforce automated canary rollbacks upon anomaly detection or insufficient evidence.
observations: Release decisions must evaluate 19 dimensions including correctness, security, quality, testing, accessibility, performance, observability, rollback capability, evidence strength, audit completeness, and risk.
The Release Agent cannot self-certify release candidates; independent verification is mandatory.
limitations: Production readiness operates locally in synthetic mode prior to live commercial cloud infrastructure activation.
recommendation: Implement Release Governance Engine, Production Readiness Model, Release Decision Engine, Production Readiness Review Engine, Release Gate State Machine, Release Contract Schema, and Synthetic Production Fixtures in EOS Control Plane.
